conditions: The message is posted in the channel #incidents.
The message's content is (or constitutes) an outage update — a message giving status/update information about an outage.
The message's author is a member of the channel #oncall-eng.
The action to take is adding the :eyes: (👀) emoji reaction to that message.

readings: The single/only message in #incidents that qualifies as an outage update
The most recent outage-update message, if more than one exists
Anyone currently listed as a member of the #oncall-eng channel (roster membership)
Whoever is currently designated/on-shift as the on-call engineer per that channel's purpose, not just any channel member

records.note: Diego posted this in #incidents about the checkout outage, and Diego is a member of #oncall-eng. Reads as the initial outage report rather than a literal follow-up update; contestable whether it counts as 'the outage update', but it is the only outage-related #incidents message from an #oncall-eng member.
Posted in #oncall-eng not #incidents; about pager handoff not the outage; Leo is not a member of #oncall-eng.
Posted in #incidents, literal follow-up outage update, but Leo is not a member of #oncall-eng.
Posted in #oncall-eng not #incidents; unrelated content about rotation swap.
Posted in #incidents with outage-update content, but Omar is not a member of #oncall-eng.
Posted in #incidents but about postmortem doc review, not the current outage; Priya is not a member of #oncall-eng.

turn2.differences: The author's three conditions match my step-1 reading closely: content about the outage update, channel is #incidents, author is a member of #oncall-eng. The only nuance is that 'member of #oncall-eng' can only be operationalized as literal channel membership since no separate on-call roster exists in the data.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Three #incidents messages concern the same outage: an initial report (Diego), and two follow-ups (Leo, Omar). Read strictly as a follow-up update, the phrase best fits Leo's or Omar's message. Read loosely as any status message about the outage, it includes Diego's. Only Diego is an #oncall-eng member, so the reading chosen determines whether any record satisfies all conditions.

Could in theory mean 'currently on-call' rather than 'in the channel roster', but the service only exposes channel membership with no separate on-call schedule, so the only workable reading is literal channel membership; this does not change which record is selected.

turn2.naturalness_note: Plausible for a bot acting for a team, though 'posted by whoever is a member of #oncall-eng' is a slightly awkward construction; a person would more likely say 'posted by someone on the on-call team' or name the person directly.
